actions.description: Pause the Gazebo world with the acknowledged /gazebo/pause_physics service; the receipt is the service acknowledgement, not a stopped-state measurement
actions.name: pause

outputs.description: True once the pause service acknowledged; not a measured stopped state
outputs.name: acknowledged

actions.description: Resume the Gazebo world with the acknowledged /gazebo/unpause_physics service; an interrupted controller goal may continue after the unpause
actions.name: resume

outputs.description: True once the resume service acknowledged
outputs.name: acknowledged

device.name: UR5 grasp and Kinect Gazebo simulation

facts.text: The shipped main.launch starts the simulation launch and the MoveIt move_group launch.
launch_simulation.launch includes gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with use_sim_time true and the world file from smart_grasping_sandbox_sample.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper appends -s libgazebo_ros_api_plugin.so unless that plugin is already present in the arguments.
GazeboRosApiPlugin initializes the ROS node with the name gazebo.
GazeboRosApiPlugin advertises its services on a private node handle named '~'.
advertiseServices creates the relative pause_physics and unpause_physics services with the std_srvs/Empty type.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
GazeboRosApiPlugin advertises rosgraph_msgs/Clock on the absolute /clock topic.
GazeboRosApiPlugin connects publishSimTime to the world update-begin event.
publishSimTime reads world_->SimTime() and publishes it as rosgraph_msgs/Clock.
JointStateController advertises sensor_msgs/JointState on the relative joint_states name through the root node handle.
The shipped joint-state controller configuration sets the controller type and publish_rate 50.
The shipped controller_utils.launch loads the joint-state controller configuration and spawns the joint_state_controller.
launch_simulation.launch loads arm_controller_ur10.yaml and spawns arm_controller, then loads gripper_gazebo_trajectory.yaml and spawns hand_controller.
arm_controller_ur10.yaml, which launch_simulation.launch loads, names six joints in the order shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint and wrist_3_joint.
launch_simulation.launch sets robot_description from ur_with_kinect.xacro.
ur_with_kinect.xacro includes model2.urdf and kinect.xacro.
model2.urdf declares arm_to_finger1 and arm_to_finger2 as prismatic joints.
model2.urdf loads the gazebo_ros_control plugin with DefaultRobotHWSim.
launch_simulation.launch declares gui with default true and paused with default false.
move_generic_model.py's move_model pauses physics, sets the model state and then unpauses physics through g_unpause when pause_physics is true.
ur5_bringup.launch takes a robot_ip argument for the IP of the robot controller.
Robotiq85Gripper opens a serial port, by default /dev/ttyUSB0 at 115200 baud.
The shipped model2.urdf declares the six arm joints as revolute joints with a position limit from -3.14159265359 to 3.14159265359 rad.
The Kinect's gazebo_ros_openni_kinect plugin publishes rgb/image_raw, depth/image_raw, depth/points and the two camera-info topics under its camera name.

determinism.notes: Event-driven contract fake with no Gazebo physics, controller, MoveIt planner or wall-clock pacing; placeholder clock and joint samples do not establish trajectory or state replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free contract transport: it answers the declared /clock, /joint_states, /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/unpause_physics endpoints and runs no Gazebo, ODE physics, gazebo_ros_control, MoveIt, contacts, sensors or wall-clock loop
the clock, joint names, joint positions, velocities and efforts are placeholders; they do not prove motion, arrival, grasp or stopped state
the fake's pause handler flips a local flag; it does not pause a simulator, does not cancel a pending controller goal and provides no stopped-state measurement
the /clock and /joint_states fake publications go silent while paused, matching the upstream world-update and controller update paths, but the fake does not model publish rates or latencies

anything with access to Gazebo can undo the pause: the GUI that launch_simulation.launch starts by default, and the vendored spawn_robot_tools move_model, which unpauses physics after moving a model when called with pause_physics (its own launch files, not the shipped main.launch)

the spawned arm (model2.urdf through ur_with_kinect.xacro) uses the ur10 meshes and UR10 link offsets (model2.urdf:55, 108, 139) and the launch loads arm_controller_ur10.yaml, although the repository and its paths name a UR5; /joint_states also carries the two prismatic finger joints

the clone vendors real-hardware drivers that this package does not bind: ur_modern_driver with ur_bringup launch files for a UR arm at a robot_ip, and robotiq_85_driver, which opens a serial port for a Robotiq 2F-85; on such a graph /joint_states reads the real arm while /gazebo/pause_physics does not exist, so the e-stop fails with the latch held

the package exposes only the simulation pause/resume services and the two explicit observations; the arm trajectory controllers, MoveIt planning, the Kinect image and point-cloud streams, the gripper command topics and the remaining Gazebo services are NOT COVERED
no real ROS graph, Gazebo, MoveIt, simulator or hardware was contacted; evidence is F0 contract_checked only

measures.description: Read one /clock sample from the Gazebo world-update publication; the topic is silent while paused and this is an explicit observation, not the resource snapshot
measures.name: read_sim_clock

measures.description: Read one /joint_states sample from the joint-state controller; the topic is silent while paused and this is an explicit observation, not the resource snapshot
measures.name: read_joint_state

safe_state.description: The acknowledged /gazebo/pause_physics service pauses the Gazebo world: it stops stepping, so the clock and joint-state publications stop and the controllers cannot move the arm until something unpauses it (the resume command, the Gazebo GUI that the shipped launch opens, or another client). This is not a stopped-state measurement; a pending trajectory goal continues after an unpause.
